audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] tells you Vladimir will "Sanguine Pool through your Tongue Lash stun and Devour to waste both cooldowns", and mid says the Pool "dodges both your Tongue Lash stun and the Devour swallow entirely". Sanguine Pool removes nothing that has already landed, and it cannot be cast while he is stunned or suppressed.
audit.why: This is the difference between a lane you cannot win and a lane you win by baiting one button. Pool is a pre-emptive dodge — he has to read the commit and press it BEFORE the stun connects. Once Tongue Lash lands its 1.5 seconds, he is stuck there for the whole thing, and Devour after it is uncontestable.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool (28/25/22/19/16s, no cast time, 2s untargetable) dodges the cast; it never escapes a stun or a suppression that has already applied.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every instruction in the entry is "bait the Pool" and not one of them says what baiting it is worth.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28 seconds at rank 1 — one of the longest basic-ability cooldowns Tahm Kench faces in the top lane — and Vladimir usually leaves it at one point for a long time while he maxes Q or E. A baited Pool is not a small window, it is most of a wave.
audit.corrected: A baited rank-1 Pool buys you 28 seconds. That is the number the whole lane plan hangs on.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is described only as unavoidable chip — "Drip Tides of Blood E poke onto you between CS", "every E tick slows you". Nothing mentions that its bolts are blocked by units.
audit.why: Riot's own text says it "can be blocked by enemy units". Standing inside your own minion wave means the wave eats bolts that would otherwise all land on you, while Tongue Lash's 900 range still reaches him. That turns his safest farming pattern into a losing one, and it is free.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood bolts are absorbed by units between you and him — poke from inside your own wave rather than from open ground.
sources: League Wiki — Vladimir: Tides of Blood

audit.why: The packet flagged "Crimson Rush" in the early paragraph as a probable mis-name for "Crimson Pact". It is a false positive — Crimson Rush is a real, separate mechanic on Transfusion. It charges over Transfusion's cooldown and at two charges Vladimir gains a movement-speed surge; casting Transfusion during that surge deals 85% increased damage and heals for more. The visible speed burst is the tell that his next Q is the big one, which is worth knowing and is not written down anywhere.
audit.corrected: Crimson Rush is genuine. Watch for the movement-speed surge — that is the empowered Transfusion coming.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] ("Lvl 3"), mid and whys[2] all describe the level-3 pattern as "3-stack stun into Devour". Devour is the ultimate and arrives at 6.
audit.why: It matters more here than in most matchups, because the entry then reasons about whether Pool can dodge "both" — a question that does not arise for another three levels. At 3 the play is bait Pool, land the stun, take the auto chain.
audit.corrected: Level 3: bait Pool, land the 1.5s stun, auto chain. Level 6 adds Devour on the end of it.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and late call Tahm Kench's W "Abyssal Voyage" and use it to "rotate for advantages elsewhere" and "globally undo his splitpush".
audit.why: There is no such ability in the current kit. Abyssal Dive is a 1.35-second channel into a 1000-1200 range blink on 21/20/19/18/17s. Nothing about it answers a Vladimir splitpush, and a player who plans around a global he does not have will simply be absent from the map.
audit.corrected: Devour is the level-6 answer; Abyssal Dive is a short telegraphed engage. Splitpush is answered by rotating early on foot.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Abyssal Dive

audit.why: Mercury's Treads, Spirit Visage and early anti-heal are right. Transfusion is his sustain engine and Hemoplague heals him for every champion it hits, so Grievous Wounds applied before the extended fight rather than during it is correct guidance.

edits.before: Your 3-stack stun into Devour combo comes online — but Vladimir can Sanguine Pool through both, so bait the Pool first before you commit the full chain.
edits.after: Your 3-stack stun comes online — Vladimir can only Pool it pre-emptively, and at rank 1 Sanguine Pool is a 28-second cooldown, so bait it and the wave is yours.

edits.after: Poke from inside your own wave — the units between you soak Tides of Blood bolts and Tongue Lash still reaches

edits.before: Bait out Sanguine Pool on a false commit, then immediately chain the real Tongue Lash stun into Devour before it comes back up
edits.after: Bait Sanguine Pool with a false commit — it runs 28/25/22/19/16s, so baiting a rank-1 Pool buys nearly half a minute

edits.before: At level 1 you have the range advantage — Tongue Lash outranges Vladimir's Q by a wide margin, so step up to the minion wave, slow him every time he walks up to last-hit, and deny him easy Q Crimson Rush stacks. He cannot pool at level 1 so this is your cleanest window to make him feel the lane. At level 2 you pick up An Acquired Taste stacking in earnest: slow him twice, then threaten the third-hit stun to force him back under tower and lose CS. Do not overextend expecting a free kill — he is farming stacks on you too, and his Q sustain starts chipping your bar.
edits.after: At level 1 you have the range advantage — Tongue Lash outranges Vladimir's Q by a wide margin, so step up to the minion wave, slow him every time he walks up to last-hit, and watch for the Crimson Rush speed surge, which is the tell that his next Transfusion hits 85% harder. He cannot pool at level 1 so this is your cleanest window to make him feel the lane. At level 2 you pick up An Acquired Taste stacking in earnest: slow him twice, then threaten the third-hit stun to force him back under tower and lose CS. Do not overextend expecting a free kill — his Q sustain starts chipping your bar.

edits.before: Level 3 is where the math gets honest: your 3-stack stun-into-Devour combo is theoretically lethal on an isolated Vladimir, but Sanguine Pool is also online and it dodges both your Tongue Lash stun and the Devour swallow entirely, resetting your stacks to zero and burning your cooldowns. Never hard-commit the full chain cold — throw a fake all-in or a Tongue Lash slow to bait the Pool, watch for the puddle animation to end, then immediately land the real stun and Devour before he can act. At level 6 his ult adds a massive empowered E burst window and he becomes a genuine all-in threat himself; respect the R-E combination when your health is below half and use Abyssal Voyage to rotate for advantages elsewhere rather than forcing a winning duel that the pool can always interrupt.
edits.after: Level 3 is where the math gets honest: your 3-stack stun is live, and Sanguine Pool is the only thing that answers it — but it answers it only in advance. He has to read the commit and press it BEFORE Tongue Lash connects; once the 1.5 seconds land he can no longer cast anything at all. So never hard-commit the chain cold: throw a fake all-in or a bare Tongue Lash slow to draw the Pool out, watch the puddle end, then walk in and land the real stun. At rank 1 that single bait is worth 28 seconds of a Vladimir with no answer. At level 6 Devour joins the chain and his Hemoplague adds a 4-second window where everything hits you 10% harder; respect the R-E combination below half health, and poke from inside your own minions so the wave eats his Tides of Blood bolts.

edits.before: Once Vladimir finishes Rylai's the lane calculus flips permanently: every Tides of Blood E tick slows you so he can perpetually kite your gap-close and keep you from reaching three An Acquired Taste stacks without burning Flash, and his Q sustain heals back whatever you managed to poke in. Your job is no longer to kill him — it is to peel your carries with Devour, absorb his ult with Thick Skin grey health converted into a shield via E activation, and use Abyssal Voyage to globally undo his splitpush or set up Baron skirmishes where your point-and-click lockdown matters more than raw damage.
edits.after: Once Vladimir finishes Rylai's the lane calculus flips permanently: every Tides of Blood tick slows you so he can perpetually kite your gap-close and keep you from reaching three An Acquired Taste stacks without burning Flash, and his Q sustain heals back whatever you managed to poke in. Your job is no longer to kill him — it is to peel your carries with Devour, absorb his ult with Thick Skin grey health converted into a shield via E activation, and rotate early to Baron and drake skirmishes where your point-and-click lockdown matters more than raw damage.

edits.before: His Sanguine Pool is online and dodges both your stun and Devour if he reads the commit — bait Pool first or the combo whiffs and resets your stacks.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool dodges the stun only if he reads the commit early — once the 1.5s stun lands he can no longer cast it, so a bait is worth 28 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: His level 6 R empowers Tides of Blood and gives him a credible all-in at low health; you get Abyssal Voyage for global pressure, making this a genuine skill read on when to fight versus rotate.
edits.after: Hemoplague marks you for 4 seconds and raises everything you take by 10% before it detonates; you get Devour, which ends any Vladimir it lands on because Pool comes too late.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Dodges your combo. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool (28/25/22/19/16s, 2s untargetable): a pre-emptive dodge only — once your stun has landed he can no longer cast it at all. Bait it and you own the next 20-28 seconds.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Sanguine Pool: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Bait Sanguine Pool, then run the pattern: it is 28s at rank 1 and it only saves him if he presses it early. Poke from inside your own wave.

edits.before: Devour deletes him from the fight — or you from his. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Vladimir's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Devour lands and Sanguine Pool has no answer to it. Hemoplague amps all damage you take by 10% for 4 seconds first.

edits.before: Track Vladimir's Sanguine Pool: Dodges your combo. Bait it. When it is down — Q-AA + R him.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool is a pre-emptive dodge — land the 1.5s stun first and he can no longer cast it.

notes: This is the only sub-50% matchup in my slice (49.8% over 1253 games) and the chart already reflects it, so I left the sides alone. The biggest single correction is that Sanguine Pool cannot escape a stun or a suppression that has already applied — the entry treated it as an escape from the completed combo, which made the lane look unwinnable when it is actually decided by one bait. Champion-wide issues seen again here: 182 "Abyssal Voyage" occurrences across champ-data/content/tahmkench.js (pre-rework ultimate; current W is Abyssal Dive, no global), and Devour promised at levels 1-5 when it is the ultimate. The packet's "Crimson Rush" suspectNames hit is a false positive — it is a real Transfusion mechanic, distinct from the Crimson Pact passive. No WKM_LINES issues seen.
